problem: Prior image-goal navigation methods fall short in one of three ways. End-to-end RL agents generalize poorly to unseen photorealistic scenes. SLAM/topological methods such as Neural Topological SLAM need pose and/or depth sensors and hand-crafted modules. Memory-based methods either need human pre-exploration of the test scene (SPTM) or were shown only on synthetic data (Scene Memory Transformer).
motivation: End-to-end RL is easier to transfer across simulators and tasks than modular SLAM pipelines, but in photorealistic Gibson scenes RL overfits badly because the inputs are high-dimensional and there are few training scenes. Agents also need some memory of places visited within an episode to explore efficiently. The authors observe that a vanilla RL baseline, trained long enough (500M steps rather than 25M) and with data augmentation, is already very strong. Adding a self-supervised compact memory, read through attention, should improve it further without any pose or depth input.
key_idea: Train a self-supervised siamese reachability network (temporal-distance labels from random-walk trajectories), use it to insert novel panoramic observations into an episodic memory, and let an end-to-end DD-PPO policy read that memory through a transformer-style attention module, all from RGB only.
insight: Much of the gain comes from RL hygiene: data augmentation (random crop + color jitter) adds about +12% overall SPL over the vanilla target-driven RL baseline (Fig. 4). With augmentation, the no-memory baseline alone already beats NTS by about +12% overall SPL. The attention-read episodic memory adds another +6% overall SPL on top. Several other results show the same pattern: generalization and training length dominate. The vanilla RL baseline reaches 0.37 SPL at 500M steps, far above its reported 25M-step number. The train/test SPL gap shrinks from about 65% to about 40% with augmentation and to about 15% with 150 extra (lower-quality) scans (Fig. 6). Panoramic input is essential: 1 view gives 0.08 SPL versus 0.36 with 4 views (Table III). Summing per-view features, which makes the embedding rotation-invariant, trains the reachability net better than concatenating them (Fig. 8). A memory persisting across 100 episodes in the same scene helps most on long episodes (+2.7% SPL on hard, +2.3% on extra, +0.9% on easy).
method: Data augmentation: random crop (min scale 0.8) and color jitter (0.2 for brightness/contrast/saturation/hue), applied independently per view to both current and goal panoramas. It is applied separately at action sampling and in the PPO forward-backward pass, and also when training the reachability net.

Navigation policy: a shared ResNet18 encodes each of v=4 panoramic RGB views (128x128). Current-view features are concatenated, passed through an FC layer, then a 2-layer LSTM together with previous actions to give w_obs. Goal-view features are summed, which makes the goal embedding rotation-invariant (w_goal). The concatenation w_joint goes to an FC action head.

Reachability (state-embedding) network: a siamese ResNet18 g (view features summed) plus an FC comparator f with 2x512 ReLU hidden layers. It predicts whether two observations are within k=10 steps in a random-walk trajectory (1 trajectory of 5k steps per training scene, 360k steps total, 144k pairs). It is trained with SGD for 30 epochs, adapted from Episodic Curiosity through Reachability.

Episodic memory: at each step the current embedding g(x_t) is added to the buffer only if its max reachability score to existing memory vectors is below threshold tau (i.e., the observation is novel). Capacity is 20 and the buffer is reset every episode.

Attention module: 4 stacked transformer-like layers (4-head attention over the fixed memory set, then a feedforward sublayer), with the query initialized from a linear projection of w_joint. The output z_t^N is concatenated with w_joint before the action FC layer.
Long-term memory variant: an additional memory that persists across 100 consecutive episodes in the same scene, alongside the per-episode memory.
Training: DD-PPO for 500M steps (50k updates, 2 PPO epochs, 64-step rollouts, entropy 0.01, clip 0.2, Adam lr 9e-5). Reward is success + decrease in geodesic distance + slack penalty.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 encoder + 2-layer LSTM + 4-layer/4-head attention module (trained from scratch with DD-PPO); self-supervised siamese ResNet18 reachability network for memory embeddings
setting.training_data: 72 Gibson train scenes: 648k image-goal episodes (9k per scene, 3k each for easy/medium/hard, NTS protocol), policy trained for 500M env steps. Reachability net: 72 random-walk trajectories x 5k steps = 360k steps, 144k sampled image pairs. Analysis variant 'More Scenes' adds 150 extra (poor-quality) Gibson scans.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB only (4 views, each 3x128x128) + goal panoramic RGB; no pose, no depth
setting.action_space: discrete MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 10° / STOP (reachability data collected with 1 m / 30°)
setting.privileged: none for the main model; the LT Memory variant keeps memory across 100 previous episodes in the same test scene

numbers.extra: RGB only (no pose/depth); 4-view panoramic input; trained 500M steps, 3 seeds; success radius 1 m, max 500 steps. Eval on NTS-protocol episodes over the 14 held-out Gibson scenes (paper calls them 'test'; 100 episodes per scene per difficulty = 4.2k): easy 1.5-3 m, medium 3-5 m, hard 5-10 m.

Memory SPL per difficulty, Fig. 4), train/test SPL curves with 'More Scenes' (Fig. 6), and the learning-rate sweeps (Fig. 9). The paper calls the 14 held-out Gibson scenes 'test'; they are the standard Gibson val scenes used by NTS, so split is recorded as 'val'.
results: On Gibson image-goal navigation (NTS protocol, 14 unseen scenes), the RGB-only memory-augmented agent reaches 0.69 SR / 0.56 SPL overall. The strongest baseline, NTS-D, which uses RGB + pose + depth, gets 0.63 / 0.43, so the gain is +13 SPL. Against SPTM, which uses pre-exploration of the test scene, the gain is +29 SPL. Hard-episode SPL roughly doubles (0.48 vs 0.26). The one weakness is easy-episode success, which is below NTS-D (0.78 vs 0.87). A cross-episode long-term memory raises overall SPL further, from 0.407 to 0.428, on an extended set that includes 10-15 m episodes.
limitations: Needs 500M training steps, versus 25M for the NTS baselines. The comparison is at convergence of each method, not at an equal step budget.
Lower success on easy (nearby) goals than NTS-D. Failure modes include looping, stopping too early, and missing extremely distant goals.

Evaluated only in simulation (Habitat/Gibson) with noiseless discrete actuation and 4-view panoramic RGB; no real-robot validation. The long-term memory variant relies on repeated episodes in the same scene.
